question: Can causal sizing of new trades by incremental common-factor independence reduce catastrophic drawdown while preserving more CAGR/wealth than simpler exposure reduction, with all MTS signals retained and no forced exits?
portfolio_mechanics: Reuse existing nonlevered cash-limited next-session-open entry and daily close marking. No signal rejection. No forced exit. Existing positions are never resized.

candidate_factor_rule.name: residual_variance_share20_floor25
candidate_factor_rule.at_each_entry: Using only the prior 20 completed sessions, build the equal-weight return series of currently active unique underlying tickers. Regress the candidate ticker returns on that active-portfolio common-factor series with intercept. multiplier=max(0.25,1-R_squared). If insufficient history or fewer than 3 active tickers, multiplier=1.0.
candidate_factor_rule.same_day_causality: All entries on a session use portfolio membership existing before that session's new entries.

null_controls: UNIFORM_MATCHED: a constant multiplier chosen only to match factor-aware average gross exposure, not performance
CONCURRENCY_MATCHED: causal inverse-concurrency entry sizing with one scalar chosen only to match factor-aware average gross exposure, not performance
decision_rule: Factor-aware is promising only if it improves the CAGR/wealth-versus-drawdown tradeoff relative to BOTH matched-exposure nulls. If drawdown improvement is explained by lower exposure or factor-aware loses to either simple matched null, kill this formulation.
